description: Open call dedicated to color and its absence. Any approach to constructing the color space of the image is welcome — soft pastels, aggressive red, B&W silhouettes. Color (or its absence) must be a key element. Online exhibition April 10–25, 2026.

title: Daylight Photo Awards 2026
description: Photography competition recognizing outstanding photographic work. Top prize includes cash award and creation of a digital portfolio. Juror picks receive international marketing promotion and the opportunity to collaborate with Daylight on a monograph. Winners announced August 2026.

title: Fotografiska HOME — Global Open Call
description: Global open call exploring home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. Selected works exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Guest curator: James Nachtwey. Submit up to 3 images. Lens-based photography only, no AI.

title: The Idle Class — Photography Issue
description: Open call for photographers of all genres to submit work for the upcoming Photography Issue of The Idle Class Magazine. Submit via email with name, description, and files.

title: Berlin Photo Awards 2026
description: International photography competition with 24 categories including Portrait, Landscape, Street, Fine Art, Wildlife, Drone, Smartphone, and more. Winners exhibited at ERSTERERSTER Gallery in Berlin and published in the official Winners Photobook.
ai: AI editing OK, fully generated not accepted

title: Galleri Format — Window Exhibition 2026
description: Open call for artists working in the broad field of photography for the 6th edition of the Window Exhibition at Galleri Format, Malmö. Exhibition runs June 12 – August 9, 2026.

title: Griffin Museum — Handmade Photobook Exhibition 2026
description: 2nd annual exhibition for handcrafted photobooks where the artist's hand shapes the object itself. Submit handmade photobooks via CaFE. Juror: Caleb Cain Marcus of Luminosity Lab.
jury: Caleb Cain Marcus, Luminosity Lab

title: Provoke USA — Open Call
description: Open call for a photography zine inspired by the Japanese Provoke movement — destabilizing certainty and revealing a world beyond conventional language. International submissions welcome. No AI-generated images. Submit via email with your Instagram handle. Name files with your name (e.g. JohnDoe 1).

title: Hariban Award 2026
description: International collotype competition combining 170-year-old analogue printing with contemporary photography. Submit 12 black-and-white photographs. Grand Prize: funded two-week residency in Kyoto collaborating with master collotype printers, solo exhibition, and publication in official catalogue. Juror's Choice and Benrido Award winners receive catalogue publication and free Collotype Academy course.
jury: Diane Dufour, Founder & Artistic Director, LE BAL Paris; Erin O'Toole, Curator & Head of Photography, SFMOMA; KIM Jeong Eun, Founder, THE REFERENCE Seoul; Leo Rongone, Photographer & CEO, Moncler

title: Dark Frames III — Carlotta Gallery
description: Black and white photography virtual exhibition. A continuation of the inquiry into monochrome photography — absence of colour as a space for deeper perception. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.

title: Flora — Carlotta Gallery
description: Nature photography virtual exhibition exploring the quiet intensity of plant life. From delicate details to expansive landscapes of growth. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.

title: Europe — Carlotta Gallery
description: Photography virtual exhibition exploring Europe as a continuous negotiation between tradition and innovation, memory and experimentation. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.

title: Candid — Carlotta Gallery
description: Candid photography virtual exhibition. The art of attention — rooted in presence, patience, and trust in the unfolding moment. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.

title: Summer — Carlotta Gallery
description: Summer photography virtual exhibition. Summer is experienced differently across the world — intensity, brightness, stillness, or transformation. Submit up to 3 images via email. Selected work shown in virtual exhibition with catalogue and certificate.

title: Paradajs Photo Fest 2026 — Welcome to Paradise
description: International photography open call exploring paradise in original, unconventional ways. Submit single photographs or series. Grand Prix winner receives €2,000, a one-month residency in Banská Štiavnica (fall 2026), production support, and a solo exhibition in 2027. 10 finalists shown in group exhibition.
jury: Jano Viazo, CEO, Paradajs Photo; Zuzana Pustaiová, Photographer & Editor; Branislav Štěpánek, Curator; Vanda Mesiariková, Photographer

title: Beautiful Bizarre Art Prize — MPB Photography Award 2026
description: International art prize (9th year) for representational photography in analogue or digital media. Submit fine art photography with only minor digital post-processing. 1st prize receives $3,000 cash, exhibition at Modern Eden Gallery in San Francisco, artwork published in December 2026 issue, in-depth interview, and 12-month Artist Directory listing. 2nd prize $1,000, 3rd prize $500 — all winners exhibit at Modern Eden. No AI-generated work accepted.

title: FotoDoc Photo Contest 2026
description: International documentary photography contest with three categories: Single Image (1–3 photos), Photo Essay (6–8 photos), and Portfolio (10–15 photos). Free to submit; $29 publication fee only if selected. 60 finalists published in festival catalog. 25 winners exhibited at FotoDoc Festival in São Paulo in November 2026. Overall Portfolio winner receives trophy, airfare, and accommodation to attend the festival. No AI-generated images accepted.

title: SUB(SCAPE) — Manifest Gallery Season 22
description: Themed group exhibition exploring what lies beneath the visible — structural, psychological, geological, social, or conceptual systems that sustain or destabilize the world above. Open to all media including photography. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium. One work selected for a $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Artists receive 70% on sales. Exhibition at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, July 10 – August 7, 2026. 22nd season of this nonprofit creative research gallery.

title: Artadia Awards 2026 — New York City
description: Unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists including photographers. Three awardees receive $15,000 each. Two-round jury process: curators review applications, then conduct 45-minute virtual studio visits with 6 finalists. Non-selected finalists receive honorariums. Artadia runs awards in 7 US cities throughout the year — NYC deadline April 1, with San Francisco (May–June), Boston (Aug–Sep), Atlanta (Sep–Oct), and Houston (Oct–Nov) following. Past awardees include artists featured in the Whitney Biennial and Prospect New Orleans.

title: XII Premio Internacional de Fotografía Jalón Ángel
description: 12th edition of this international photography prize organized by Universidad San Jorge in Zaragoza, Spain. Three categories: Portrait (spontaneous or posed), Travel (landscapes, cultures, traditions), and Migration & Borders (human movement, territorial and cultural limits). One photograph per category. No AI, no heavy retouching, RAW files may be requested. Winners announced June 25. Named after Jalón Ángel (1898–1976), one of Spain's most celebrated portrait photographers.

title: Bethany Arts Community — Fall Multidisciplinary Residency 2026
description: Two-week artist residency in Ossining, New York (Sep 22 – Oct 6, 2026) for 12 artists across all disciplines including photography, visual arts, film, writing, and performance. Residents receive a $450 stipend, private studio, room and board, and 3 meals daily. Each artist facilitates one community program during the residency. Requires one letter of recommendation and one reference. Funded by the National Endowment for the Arts and New York State Council on the Arts.

title: Diane Dammeyer Fellowship in Photographic Arts and Social Awareness 2026/27
org: Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia
description: Fellowship supporting socially engaged photographers in creating work within a community. The fellow partners with a Chicago-based community organization to address human rights, social, economic, or cultural issues through photography. September–June commitment with flexible hours. Culminates in a public exhibition and/or publication at MoCP. Preference for Chicago-based projects. Requires MFA in photography or related field, or BA with 5 years post-degree creative practice. Two professional references required.

title: XIX Premio de Fotografía Fundación ENAIRE 2026
description: 19th edition of this prestigious photography prize, running since 2005, in collaboration with PHotoESPAÑA. Open theme — submit up to 3 artistic photographs (digital or analog). Two-phase process: digital submission, then 30 finalists present physical prints (1x1m to 3x3m). Winning works join the ENAIRE Contemporary Art Collection. Finalists and winners exhibit at Naves de Gamazo in Santander during PHotoESPAÑA 2026. AI-generated images not allowed.

title: International Photography and Football Open Call 2026
description: International open call for photographers to capture football/soccer in any form — packed stadiums, dirt fields, color or black and white, cameras or phones. Winners exhibited alongside the Annie Leibovitz Futbol 2026 exhibition at the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City. Submit 1–3 images. Judged on originality, impact, and narrative quality.
jury: Annie Leibovitz, Photographer; Pablo Ortiz Monasterio, Photographer & Editor; Carlos Cuarón, Filmmaker; Ana Hop, Photographer

title: Women Photograph + Leica Documentary Grant 2026
description: Grant supporting women, nonbinary, and transgender documentary photographers. The $10,000 Leica grant supports ongoing documentary projects — submit 20 images showing substantial completed work. Seven additional $5,000 grants available for new or in-progress visual journalism projects. Applications open April 1.

title: Lenscratch Student Prize 2026
description: Annual prize supporting emerging student photographers. First Prize $2,000 cash plus year-long mentorship with Aline Smithson, portfolio reviews with curators, $500 Freestyle Photo gift certificate, and exhibition. Second Prize $1,000, Third $750, four Honorable Mentions $500 each.
jury: Aline Smithson, Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Lenscratch; Alexa Dilworth, Former Publishing Director, CDS at Duke University; Kris Graves, Director, Kris Graves Projects; Karen Haas, Lane Curator of Photographs, Museum of Fine Arts Boston; Yorgos Efthymiadis, Founder, The Curated Fridge; Hamidah Glasgow, Curator & Former Director, Center for Fine Art Photography

title: Lenscratch Motherhood Exhibition
description: Online exhibition exploring all dimensions of motherhood — traditional mother-child relationships, chosen families, caregiving, absence, loss, resilience, and inheritance. Submit one image via Google Form (72dpi, 1000px long side).

title: Lenscratch Fatherhood Exhibition
description: Online exhibition exploring fatherhood as an evolving role shaped by culture, responsibility, tenderness, and family expectations. Submit one image via Google Form (72dpi, 1000px long side).

title: Lenscratch Fault Lines: America Exhibition
description: Online exhibition examining tensions, fractures, and transformations across America — resistance, social change, protest, activism, justice, identity, power, and freedom. Submit one image via Google Form (72dpi, 1000px long side). Timed for July 4th.

title: SE Center for Photography — Magic of Light
description: Virtual juried exhibition exploring light and shadow as the foundation of photography. Submit up to 15 images. Juror: Wendi Schneider. 35–40 images selected for virtual gallery. 0% commission on sales. All photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. Analog and digital welcome.

title: photoED Magazine — Home VS Away (Issue #76)
description: Fine art photography projects investigating the idea of home, the experience of being away, or the tension between the two. 10 selected projects published in print edition, 25 more in digital companion. Contributors receive printed copies with worldwide shipping. Free for subscribers and economically challenged artists.

title: photoED Magazine — Real VS Imagined
description: Fine art photography projects engaging with what is real versus what is imagined. 10 selected projects published in print edition, 25 more in digital companion. Contributors receive printed copies with worldwide shipping. Free for subscribers.

title: LUMA Rencontres Dummy Book Award 2026
description: Annual award supporting publication of an unpublished photobook dummy. Special attention to experimental and innovative editorial forms. Winner's dummy and shortlisted entries exhibited at Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026. €25,000 production budget for the winning book.

title: 8th Chelsea International Photography Competition
description: International photography competition with exhibition at Agora Gallery in Chelsea, New York. 30 photographers selected for collective exhibition. Open to all genres and camera types. Five winners receive $500 cash each plus exhibition and online promotion.

title: Creatura Magazine Issue 02 — What We Call Home
description: Open call for Issue 02 of this indie print magazine exploring the idea of home — not only as a physical space but as an emotional territory. Selected photographs featured in a collective section of the print edition.

title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #137 — Open Theme
description: No theme — all fine art and documentary photography welcome. Submit up to 12 photographs. One submission per person per issue. Featured artist selected from submissions. Published since 2004.

title: Photo Trouvée Virtual Artist Residency — Spring 2026
description: 10-week virtual residency (April 24 – June 26, 2026) for artists who work with or are inspired by found/family photographs. Weekly Zoom calls, bio/statement workshops, artist talks, group feedback, accountability groups. Only 9 artists selected. Partial scholarships available.

title: HNDL Magazine — PRIDE Issue
description: Submissions for the PRIDE issue of HNDL Magazine, an indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. Accepting art, poetry, creative nonfiction, prose, photography, and zines. Especially seeking candid photography and creative nonfiction. Written pieces max 4 pages, no PDFs. Unpaid — contributors receive a printed copy.

title: Off The Clock 2026
description: 15th annual curated photo competition showcasing personal work. Juried by Chris Pichler, Founder and Publisher of Nazraeli Press, who selects 100 winning images. Winners receive a printed and PDF catalog, online gallery feature, social media exposure, and framed exhibition at an industry gala in Southern California. No categories, no series restrictions, no creation date restrictions — just your finest personal photography. APA members pay $20/image. No AI-generated content.

title: The Female Show 2026
description: Group exhibition of national and international female artists at Munich Art Gallery in the Kunstareal, running October 15 – November 14, 2026, including Lange Nacht der Münchner Museen. Curated by Josephine Kaiser & Team. Seeks contemporary art by women beyond gender stereotypes and thematic clichés. Smaller formats preferred (up to 50×50 cm). Submit a PDF (max 5 pages, 5 MB) with short CV, artist statement, ~5 example images, Instagram and website. No participation or exhibition fees — only international shipping at artist's expense. Applications accepted in English or German.

title: Open Call — Il Reportage in Italia
description: Open call for the 6th edition of Festival del Reportage in Ascoli Piceno (June 26–28, 2026). Seeking reportage photography projects made in Italy — completed or in progress, 15–25 images. At least some photos must be taken after January 1, 2025. Submit via Google Form with a file-sharing link (WeTransfer, Google Drive, etc.). Winner receives €500 cash prize, projection of work at the festival, and full hospitality including travel within Italy, accommodation, and meals. No restrictions on nationality, age, or experience.

title: 100 Emerging Artworks of 2026
description: Annual international open call selecting 100 emerging and mid-career artists for a hardcover collector's book distributed globally via Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and art bookstores. All mediums accepted including photography. Submit up to 20 artworks. Top winner receives $1,000 cash prize, 4-page feature spread, and glass trophy. 2nd and 3rd place get 4-page spreads and trophies. All 100 selected artists receive book publication, certificate, and international distribution. Early bird deadline April 4 with reduced fees. 4th edition, previous collaborators include The Jealous Curator and Singulart.

title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2026
description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Submit 10–20 images plus project statement (530 words) and bio via CaFE (Call for Entry). Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Winners donate two prints to NOPA's permanent collection and submit a final report by August 2026.

title: Luz e Sombra — National Photography Competition
description: National photography competition exploring the relationship between light and shadow across themes of heritage, nature, architecture, and daily life. Submit a series of 6 photographs with a conceptual synopsis (1,500 chars) and bio (1,000 chars). Six finalists selected — works published in an artist-edition book, shown in a traveling exhibition at three venues, and featured in the Égide digital gallery. Open to professional and amateur photographers who are Portuguese citizens or residents of Portugal.

title: CPG Mentorship Programme 2026
description: 1:1 mentoring programme pairing artists with established photographers, curators, and mediators for four meetings over six months (May–October 2026), in person or online. Mentees receive CHF 500 project support and free access to two online masterclasses. 2026 mentors include Hannah Darabi, Yann Mingard, Abdo Shanan, Holly Roussell, Jermaine Francis, and others. Open to professional artists and photographers (including self-taught) not enrolled in another programme or academic course. Fluency required in one of: French, English, Italian, Arabic, German, Farsi, or Mandarin.

title: New Wave Photography Award 2026
description: Biennial award for emerging photographers, judged by 16 international curators and professionals from Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore. Submit a series of 15–25 images (created after 2021) with artist statement in Chinese and English (500 words each). Grand Prize receives TWD 100,000 (~$3,000) plus exhibition. Applicants must not have held solo exhibitions at museums, commercial galleries, or art fairs, and no more than 5 group shows. Students and persons with disabilities pay reduced fee of TWD 600.

title: Solo Statement — Doesn't Play Well with Others
description: One-night solo takeover of Bushwick Gallery in Brooklyn — a full transformation of the space by a single artist. No shared walls, no compromise. All mediums welcome including photography, installation, performance, and digital. No prior gallery experience required. Submit artist statement (150 words), creative vision for the space, 3–5 recent work images, and two artistic influences. Gallery provides professional photography, press release, and promotional support. Exhibition April 17, 2026.

title: The Woman Artist Award — 6th Edition
description: Juried award for women artists working in any visual arts medium including photography. Winner receives $500 cash prize, glass trophy, interview feature in hardcover coffee table book, website interview, one-year portfolio feature on Women in Arts Network (global directory for women artists), and one-year subscription to Arts to Hearts print + digital magazine. No specific theme — submit your best work. 6th edition.

title: Solstice Magazine Issue 71 — Editorial Submissions
description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 71 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. Send editorial submissions via email.

title: LSI Women in Photography Grant 2026
description: Grant for women photographers to complete an in-progress personal project. Theme: Where We Stand — seeking work rooted in lived experience, proximity, trust-based relationships, and ethical representation. Submit 10 images, artist statement, project proposal, and budget via Picter. Winner receives $10,000 plus a new Leica camera and lens from Leica North America. Limited to first 100 applicants. Open globally, no Leica camera or LSI membership required.

title: Roma E'Festival — Street Photography Awards 2026
description: International street photography contest, 3rd edition. Five categories: Single Image (color/open), Black & White, Smartphone, Photographic Project (5–15 images), and AI-Generated (separate judging). Top 3 finalists per category receive prizes from partners Fotodiego, Fowa, and Ricoh GR. All finalists exhibited at Officine Fotografiche in Rome (October 16–18, 2026) and published in international catalogue. Multi-category passes available. No generative AI in street categories.

title: Dyonyzine Issue 06 — Second Helpings
description: Asian-American-founded creative arts magazine accepting submissions for Issue 06 themed around food — a meal is never just a meal. Accepting photography, visual art, drawings, paintings, digital illustrations, multimedia works, and more alongside poetry, prose, and essays. Open to all ages, backgrounds, locations, and experience levels. Volunteer-run, completely free to submit.

title: FeelsZine Issue 26 — Desire
description: Canadian creative zine accepting submissions for Issue 26 themed around desire. Accepts photography, illustration, collage, typography, and comics. Submit 1–2 works at 6.5×9.5 inches with 0.125-inch bleed. Unpaid publication. Submit via email.

title: Cut+Paste Magazine Issue 17 — Gather
description: Photography magazine Issue 17 themed around autumn gathering — harvest scenes, friends and family, cozy candlelit moments. Accepts portraits (faceless preferred), nature, landscapes, abstract, still life, urban, and macro photography. No nudity or AI art. Pays $15 base plus $5–10 per additional piece if selected.

title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Creative Wildlife
description: Submit up to 5 creative wildlife images with captions for publication in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Celestron Nature DX 12×56 binoculars (RRP £229). JPG at 300ppi.

title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Spring Landscapes
description: Submit up to 5 spring landscape images with captions for publication in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Komperdell Carbon CXP Pro walking poles (RRP £150). JPG at 300ppi.

title: Zone Magazine — Open Submissions
description: International photography zine accepting submissions year-round. No restrictions on genre. Submit up to 20 JPG images in a ZIP file (20MB max). Open to all ages worldwide.

title: Burn Magazine — Open Submissions
description: Photography magazine founded by David Alan Harvey (Magnum). Accepts photo essays, slideshows, and multimedia pieces on any subject. Submit as PDF. Images at 1080px shortest side. Features published on homepage with consideration for print.

title: Incandescent Zine — Color Film Photography
description: Bi-annual zine exclusively for color film/analog photography. Submit up to 12 color film images. No digital photography. Published by Pine Island Press, Portland, Oregon.

title: Phases Magazine — Open Submissions
description: International contemporary photography magazine publishing 3 portfolios per issue. Submit website link or low-res images.

title: Noice Magazine — Open Submissions
description: Print-to-order photography magazine with themed issues focusing on minimalism, social issues, and humor. Submit up to 10 images per themed call. Published as limited edition prints distributed worldwide.

title: Solo Exhibition May 2026
description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (May 1–31, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Photographer & Founder, All About Photo

title: SIYU Award 2026
description: Award for young Swiss photographers (formerly vfg Young Talent Award). Ten finalists exhibited in a group show at Photobastei Zurich with a published catalogue. Three cash prizes awarded through the Alois Ottiger Grant, in memory of Swiss photographer Alois Ottiger (1941–2025). Free theme, all fields of photography. Submissions must be anonymous.
jury: Virginie Otth, Photographer & Visual Artist; Bassma El Adissey, Freelance Curator; Gregor Brandli, Filmmaker & Photographer

title: Alpine Fellowship Visual Art Prize 2026
description: Annual visual art prize on the theme of JOY. Open to all visual art media including photography, painting, sculpture, video, and installation. One piece per entry, multiple entries allowed as separate submissions. Work must be entirely created without AI.
jury: Sue Grayson Ford MBE, Former Director, Serpentine Gallery & Photographers' Gallery London; Julian Spalding, Former Director of Art Galleries for Sheffield, Manchester & Glasgow

title: This Is a Person
description: Portrait photography exploring interior life over surface identity. Seeking images that suggest psychological tension, ambiguity, vulnerability, or contradiction rather than likeness alone. Intentionally selective — approximately 10–12% acceptance rate. One image per selected artist exhibited.
jury: Hossein Fardinfard, Portrait Photographer

title: Monochrome Awards 2026
description: International black and white photography competition with professional and amateur divisions across 14 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature, Portrait, Street, and Wildlife. Winners published in annual book and featured in online Winners Gallery.
jury: Kazuya Kato; Maren Klemp; Heiko Hellwig; Artur Sikora; Simona Nalepkova; Farzad Ariannejad; Paulo Monteiro; Radin Badrnia; Yugo Ito; Tomas Paule; Elhanan Simhayev; Rick Fong; Nicola Di Sario

title: Annual Photography Awards 2026
description: International photography competition (8th edition) celebrating photographers of all levels. Five main categories — Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special — with 25 subcategories. Accepts all formats, looking for bold and innovative approaches.
jury: Juliette Mills; Alex Bronfer; Carolina Rapezzi; Marc De Tollenaere; Isabella Tabacchi; Filippo Venturi; Warun Siriprachai; Diogo Baptista; Alessandra Bello; Kai Yokoyama; Annick Donkers; Richard Ansett; Apratim Saha; Jeoffrey Guillemard; Emily Kinni; Tomas Vrana; Cristina Vatielli; Jon Enoch; Nikolai Linares

title: HER.SELF
description: Online juried exhibit celebrating women in all their complexities — presence, resilience, beauty, and becoming. Open to all fine art mediums including photography. Artists receive 100% of sale price with no commission.

title: Wider Skies Magazine — Issue 1
description: New photo magazine exploring speculative futurism — not as science fiction, but as a way of noticing the near futures already forming around us. Submit up to 4 film photographs for the first issue. Looking for images that point to possible futures grounded in real life — moments of care, repair, survival, shared responsibility, quiet adaptation, or small signs of change. Film only. Free Kodak Pro 100 film available for those who need it.

title: Atlas of Ruins Vol.3 — Call for Photos
description: Submit photographs of architectural ruins from anywhere in the world for the third edition of the Atlas of Ruins book. Photos can depict ruins from any historical period — abandoned buildings, crumbling monuments, forgotten infrastructure. Three registration tiers: Early (until Apr 16, €10/1 photo, €20/up to 10), Regular (until Jul 9, €13/€25), Late (until Oct 1, €16/€30). Fees exclude VAT. All participants receive an ebook copy. Best photos from each country featured in the printed book.
requirements: JPEG, min 1200px longest edge, max 5MB, no watermarks

title: SVĚTOVA 1 Artist Residency 2026
description: One-month creative residency for an emerging visual artist in Prague. Includes private bedroom, shared 30m² studio in the gallery, production budget of approximately €820, round-trip travel, curatorial support, and opportunities for a public workshop, artist lecture, and exhibition. Open to residents of 39 European countries plus Tunisia. Must not be enrolled in educational programs during the residency. Residency runs November 1 – December 6, 2026.
requirements: CV + portfolio (single PDF, max 15 pages, under 10 MB) + cover letter or video introduction

title: Monograph No. 01
description: Open call for lens-based artists to submit a cohesive photographic project for an individual artist monograph. The selected artist receives full publication support including editing, design, printing, and marketing, plus 20% of the edition. A shortlist of 6 artists will also receive published interviews.
requirements: Cohesive body of work ready to be developed into book form

title: 37th Annual Juried Photography Show
description: Annual juried photography show in Ithaca, NY. Up to $1,000 in prizes awarded. Original work not previously exhibited at the gallery is accepted across all photographic media. Selected work exhibited May 28 through June 27, 2026.

title: Homo Technologicus
description: International call exploring the relationship between humans and technology. Seeking works investigating social, environmental, physical, cognitive, and emotional transformations brought by digital innovation. Group exhibition in Rome, November 2026.
requirements: 1-3 works (photography, digital visual design, or video)

title: Residency Program 2026
description: Two residencies for artists working in photography or photo-based media. Each provides a two-week intensive work period, $1,000 stipend, and housing in Indianapolis. Includes darkroom, studio, and digital lab access. Residencies run August through November 2026.

title: People 2026
description: International photography call exploring the human figure across all approaches including portraits, documentary, street photography, and studio work. Diverse interpretations welcome whether posed or unposed, observed or imagined. Selected work displayed in online exhibition.
requirements: No limit on submissions, fee per image

title: Nature 2026
description: Exhibition exploring how we interact with nature. Seeking images that reveal beauty, power, cruelty, and influence on daily life. Selected work displayed in Glasgow gallery, online gallery, and exhibition catalogue. Exhibition runs July 3-31, 2026.
requirements: 1-8 JPEG images, 300ppi, 3000px min on shortest side

title: Future Days 2026
description: Open theme exhibition asking photographers to represent their vision of the future, whether hopeful or fearful. Interpret the theme at a global, local, or personal level. Selected work displayed in Glasgow gallery, online gallery, and exhibition catalogue. Exhibition runs July 3-31, 2026.
requirements: 1-8 JPEG images, 300ppi, 3000px min on shortest side

title: Artist in Residence Program 2026
description: Four-week residency for artists advancing contemporary photography. Two artists selected: one slot for a Philadelphia-based artist, one open to all. Includes $3,000 honorarium, waived printer/scanner fees, $1,000 ink and paper credit, and $1,500 travel/housing reimbursement. Residencies run June through November 2026.
requirements: Letter of intent, portfolio, and CV

title: Outside the Box: Cameraless Photography
description: Exhibition seeking photographic works incorporating cameraless techniques including photograms, chemigrams, lumen prints, and composites blending camera and non-camera methods. 30-40 pieces selected for gallery exhibition and website display.

title: X ROID Bonn 2026
description: 7th edition of the international instant art expo dedicated to Polaroid and Fuji Instax photography. Three-day juried exhibition at The Stage Gallery in Bonn featuring artist talks, a Pola walk, and creative exchanges. Only original instant photographs accepted — no prints. Fee includes professional framing. Gallery takes 25% commission on sales. In media partnership with Analog Forever.
requirements: Up to 4 Polaroids or 2 large format (8x10)

title: Defiance Zine Open Call
description: Open call for Revoke Collective's first zine on the theme of Defiance. Looking for photographs that challenge, disrupt, or simply refuse. Defiance can take many forms: quiet resistance, bold rebellion, personal freedom, cultural pushback, or moments of quiet nonconformity. Not chasing polish — chasing pulse. Raw vision and unfiltered moments.

title: Les Mots du Phare Vol. 04: Futur(s)
description: Open call for black-and-white photography for Vol. 04 of Les Mots du Phare, a print publication by Linea Recta Books and Le Phare Collectif. Theme: Futur(s) — imagining what seems impossible, a tomorrow, an after, a continuation. Not the end of the world, but the courage to imagine what is possible. Selected images will be featured in the printed edition alongside text contributions from members of the collective. Submit up to 4 B&W photos combined into one PDF via email.
